# Fluent vs Omi: same pendant,different software.

Omi is an open-source pendant. Fluent is closed-source software that runs on top of it. They don't compete. They're stacked on each other.

If you bought an Omi, you can have both. Most early adopters do.

## What you're actually choosing between

### Omi (the pendant + native app)

- Open-source hardware. Hackable. Light.
- Open-source app.
- Community of developers building plugins.
- The full stack if you want to tinker.

### Fluent (software for your Omi)

- Polished iOS app. Native feel.
- Meeting notes written like a chief of staff wrote them.
- Person profiles. Calendar agent. Coach. Daily insights.
- MCP server for plugging into Claude or ChatGPT.
- The stack if you'd rather use the pendant than build on it. [...] Some Omi owners are building plugins. Some Omi owners are using the pendant and want meeting notes and follow-through. Fluent is for the second group.

## Omi and the alternatives [...] ### The app is the problem, not the pendant

Keep the Omi. Fluent pairs with it and turns what it hears into meeting notes, the commitments people made, profiles of the people you talk to, and coaching.

### You don't want a pendant at all

For meetings, your phone may be enough: Fluent records a meeting straight from your iPhone, so there is no device to buy.

## Questions

### What is the best alternative to Omi?

If you want a different device, Plaud NotePin ($159) is the most finished alternative in stock. If you like the Omi hardware but not its app, keep it and use Fluent with it.

results.title: Omi Alternatives: Wearable AI Note-Takers Compared (2026)
results.content:
- The primary hardware alternatives to Omi are the Plaud NotePin ($159), the Fieldy 3 ($129 on sale), and the Bee Pioneer ($49.99). Users who conduct meetings primarily at desks can also use software-based meeting recorders to capture computer audio directly without buying wearable hardware.
- Plaud NotePin is the most practical choice for business professionals needing up to 1,200 minutes of notes per month due to its $99.99 annual plan. Omi is the top choice for developers who require open-source code and MCP server integrations.
- For a dedicated device, we would pick Plaud NotePin or Omi. Plaud provides structured tiers for moderate workloads, while Omi provides an open-source MIT codebase, on-phone processing, and an app marketplace with over 1,000 extensions. [...] Two changes would shift our answer. If Plaud publishes open-source firmware, Omi's developer edge would shrink. If Omi introduces a mid-tier subscription priced near $100 per year, Plaud's price edge would shrink.

## The Verdict

The Plaud NotePin is the best all-around alternative to Omi for mainstream professionals. At $159 for the device, it matches Omi's 300 free monthly minutes and offers a 1,200-minute Pro tier for $99.99 a year. This makes Plaud cheaper for moderate monthly workloads than Omi Unlimited at about $270 per year. [...] The Fieldy 3 is the top alternative for high-volume users seeking low subscription overhead. At $129 on sale and $191.88 annually for unlimited transcription, Fieldy 3 costs about $78 a year less than Omi Unlimited ($191.88 against about $270). Meanwhile, Bee is the entry-level choice at $49.99 for US iPhone users, since it is iOS-only and ships only to the US.

Stay with Omi if you value open-source access, developer APIs, and custom integrations. With about 13,600 GitHub stars, an MIT license and a hosted MCP server, Omi fits programmers who want to self-host and script their own capture pipeline.

# Omi Local (Omibutfree)

The Open Source, Privacy-First Companion for Omi Devices.

Flutter Platform License Version

Features • Installation • Architecture • Roadmap

## 🚀 Overview

Omi Local is a fully functioning, self-hosted alternative to the official Omi app. It is designed for users who want full control over their data, zero monthly subscriptions, and a powerful local-first AI experience.

It connects directly to your Omi hardware (Friend/DevKit) via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and processes audio entirely on your terms—whether that's using local Whisper models on your iPhone or your own private API keys for Cloud transcription.
